PurposeThe first arm balance most people learn, and it builds real wrist, shoulder and stomach strength. Almost everyone falls forward the first several times — put a cushion in front of you and expect it.

  1. Squat down with your feet together and place your hands flat on the floor, shoulder width apart
  2. Bend your elbows slightly and rest your knees high on the backs of your upper arms
  3. Shift your weight forward onto your hands and look slightly ahead, not down
  4. Lift one foot, then the other, until only your hands touch the floor
  5. Hold for as long as you can control, then step the feet back down
ea_crow_pose

Double Pigeon Pose

Yoga

PurposeStacking the shins stretches the outside of both hips at once, which is where tightness settles in anyone who sits. Intense — sit on a cushion if the knees are far off the floor.

  1. Sit on the floor and bend one leg so the shin is parallel to the front of the mat
  2. Stack the other shin directly on top, ankle over knee and knee over ankle
  3. Sit up tall on both sitting bones
  4. Stay upright or fold slowly forward from the hips
  5. Hold for a minute, breathing into the outer hips, then swap which leg is on top
ea_double_pigeon_pose hip

Downward Dog Toe to Heel

Yoga

PurposePedalling the heels one at a time stretches each calf and hamstring separately, which is more effective than holding both still. It is also how you find out which side is tighter.

  1. Start on hands and knees, then lift the hips up and back into an inverted V
  2. Press the floor away with your hands and lengthen your spine
  3. Bend one knee and press the opposite heel toward the floor
  4. Hold for a breath, then switch, pedalling slowly between sides
  5. Continue for thirty to sixty seconds
ea_downward_dog_toe_to_heel wrist

Downward Dog with Fingers Facing Feet

Yoga

PurposeTurning the fingers backwards puts the stretch into the underside of the forearms and the wrists, which is exactly what needs to open before push-ups, front squats or handstands. Go gently.

  1. Start on hands and knees and turn both hands so the fingers point toward your feet
  2. Press the palms flat and keep the elbows soft
  3. Lift your hips up and back into a downward dog shape
  4. Take only as much weight into the hands as the wrists comfortably allow
  5. Hold for fifteen to twenty seconds, then come down and shake the wrists out
ea_downward_dog_with_fingers_facing_feet wrist

Eagle Arms Chin Into Chest

Yoga

PurposeWrapping the arms spreads the shoulder blades apart, stretching the upper back where a desk day makes it stiff. Adding the chin tuck reaches the back of the neck at the same time.

  1. Sit or stand tall and extend both arms straight in front of you
  2. Cross one arm over the other at the elbows and wrap the forearms if you can
  3. Lift the elbows to shoulder height and push the hands forward
  4. Tuck your chin toward your chest and round the upper back slightly
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then unwrap and cross the other arm on top
ea_eagle_arms_chin_into_chest

Easy Pose Neck Stretch

Yoga

PurposeReleases the sides of the neck, which carry tension from screens and from stress. Using the hand adds only a little weight — the neck needs far less force than any other area.

  1. Sit cross-legged with your spine tall and shoulders relaxed
  2. Let one hand rest on the floor beside you and press it down gently
  3. Tilt your head so the opposite ear moves toward that shoulder
  4. Rest the free hand lightly on the side of your head — do not pull
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_easy_pose_neck_stretch neck

Easy Seated Twist Pose

Yoga

PurposeRestores rotation in the spine, which is the movement the back loses first and misses most. Done sitting, so it can be fitted into a working day without a mat.

  1. Sit cross-legged with both sitting bones evenly on the floor
  2. Lengthen your spine upward before you turn
  3. Place one hand behind you and the other on the opposite knee
  4. Turn your ribs, then your shoulders, then finally your head to that side
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind and twist the other way
ea_easy_seated_twist_pose wrist

Extended Side Angle Pose

Yoga

PurposeWorks the legs while stretching the whole side of the body from the back foot to the top hand. It combines strength and length in one shape, which is why it appears in almost every sequence.

  1. Step your feet wide apart and turn the front foot out ninety degrees
  2. Bend the front knee over the ankle and keep the back leg straight
  3. Rest the front forearm on the front thigh or take the hand to the floor
  4. Reach the top arm over your ear so it makes a line with the back leg
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing into the top ribs, then change sides
ea_extended_side_angle_pose

Extended Side Angle Pose with Block

Yoga

PurposeThe block raises the floor to meet your hand, so you can hold the full shape without collapsing the chest toward the thigh. The version to use until the hips open enough for the floor.

  1. Step wide and turn the front foot out, placing a block beside the front ankle
  2. Bend the front knee over the ankle with the back leg straight
  3. Rest the front hand on the block instead of the floor
  4. Open the chest toward the ceiling and reach the top arm over your ear
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change sides
ea_extended_side_angle_pose_with_block

Gate Pose Rounding Spine Looking Up

Yoga

PurposeA side bend from a kneeling position that opens the ribs and the side of the waist, plus the inner thigh of the extended leg. It reaches the breathing muscles between the ribs, which nothing else does directly.

  1. Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg straight out to the side, foot flat
  2. Rest the same-side hand lightly on the extended leg
  3. Reach the opposite arm up and over toward the extended foot
  4. Turn your chest slightly upward and lengthen through the top ribs
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing wide, then change sides
ea_gate_pose_rounding_spine_looking_up

Gate Pose Variation Arm Extended on Side

Yoga

PurposeA gentler gate pose where the arm reaches along the leg rather than overhead, which keeps the shoulder out of it. Useful when the shoulder is sore but the side of the body still needs opening.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other leg extended straight to the side
  2. Keep the extended foot flat and the hips facing forward
  3. Slide the same-side hand down along the extended leg
  4. Let the opposite arm rest on your hip or reach softly overhead
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then swap legs
ea_gate_pose_variation_arm_extended_on_side

Half Lotus

Yoga

PurposeA seated position that opens the outside of one hip at a time and is comfortable enough to hold for a long while. Used for sitting and breathing work rather than as a stretch to push into.

  1. Sit on the floor with both legs straight out in front of you
  2. Bend one knee and place that foot on the opposite thigh, sole facing up
  3. Tuck the other foot under the opposite thigh
  4. Sit tall on both sitting bones with the hands resting on the knees
  5. Hold and breathe for a minute or more, then change which leg is on top
ea_half_lotus

Half Monkey Pose

Yoga

PurposeA hamstring stretch approached from a kneeling lunge, which lets you control the depth precisely with your hips. It is the safe route toward the full splits, and useful on its own.

  1. Start in a low lunge with one foot forward and the back knee on the mat
  2. Slide the front foot forward and straighten that leg, toes pointing up
  3. Sit your hips back over the back knee
  4. Keep your back long and hinge forward from the hips, not the spine
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then change legs
ea_half_monkey_pose

Happy Baby

Yoga

PurposeOpens the inner thighs and the lower back at the same time, in a position where the floor supports the whole spine. One of the safest hip stretches there is, which is why it suits sore backs.

  1. Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your armpits
  2. Reach up and hold the outside edges of your feet, or your shins
  3. Keep the soles of the feet facing the ceiling and the shins vertical
  4. Press the feet up into your hands and let your lower back settle onto the floor
  5. Hold for thirty seconds or longer, rocking gently if it feels good
ea_happy_baby hip

Lord of the Dance

Yoga

PurposeCombines a standing balance with a deep stretch through the front of the thigh, hip and chest. Demanding on all three at once, which is what makes it a good test of how the whole front line is moving.

  1. Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot
  2. Bend the other knee and take hold of that ankle or foot from the inside
  3. Press the lifted foot back into your hand as you hinge forward slightly
  4. Reach the opposite arm forward for balance and open your chest
  5. Hold for fifteen to thirty seconds, then come down and change sides
ea_lord_of_the_dance

Monkey Pose

Yoga

PurposeThe full front splits, which asks for length in the hamstring of one leg and the front of the hip of the other at the same time. It takes months of consistent work — use blocks and go slowly.

  1. Start in a low lunge with blocks placed either side of your hips
  2. Straighten the front leg and slide the heel forward, toes pointing up
  3. Slide the back knee backwards, keeping the hips square to the front
  4. Take your weight on the blocks and lower only as far as is comfortable
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then come out carefully and change sides
ea_monkey_pose

One Arm Cow Face Pose - Easy

Yoga

PurposeStretches the back of one shoulder and the triceps at the same time, in the overhead position that most people cannot reach comfortably. Working one arm shows plainly which side is tighter.

  1. Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed
  2. Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so the hand drops behind your head
  3. Use the other hand to hold that elbow gently
  4. Draw the elbow slightly back and toward the midline without arching your back
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then change arms
ea_one_arm_cow_face_pose_easy

Pigeon Glutes Stretch

Yoga

PurposeThe most direct stretch there is for the back of the hip, which tightens from sitting and refers pain into the lower back and down the leg. Uncomfortable, and usually worth it.

  1. From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind the same-side wrist
  2. Angle the shin across your body and slide the other leg straight back
  3. Square your hips toward the floor, using a cushion under the front hip if needed
  4. Stay upright or fold forward over the front leg
  5. Hold for a minute, breathing slowly, then change sides
ea_pigeon_glutes_stretch hip

Pigeon Pose

Yoga

PurposeOpens the back of the front hip and the front of the back hip at the same time — the two areas that between them decide how freely you walk and run. One of the most useful shapes in yoga for anyone who trains.

  1. From all fours, slide one knee forward toward the same-side hand
  2. Let the shin angle across the mat and extend the other leg straight back
  3. Keep the back leg's toes pointing straight down and the hips level
  4. Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor
  5. Hold for a minute, then press back up and change sides
ea_pigeon_pose hip

Puppy Pose

Yoga

PurposeStretches the shoulders and the upper back with the hips staying high, so the lower back is not involved. The best shape for opening overhead range if the lower back does not tolerate a deep fold.

  1. Start on hands and knees with the hips directly over the knees
  2. Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor
  3. Keep the hips stacked over the knees — do not sit back toward the heels
  4. Rest your forehead or chin on the mat and let the chest sink
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, breathing into the upper back
ea_puppy_pose

Pyramid Pose - Parsvottanasana

Yoga

PurposeA standing hamstring stretch with the hips square, which stops the pelvis from twisting to make the stretch easier. That squareness is what makes it more effective than reaching for one toe.

  1. Step one foot forward about a leg's length, both legs straight
  2. Turn the back foot out slightly and square both hips to the front
  3. Lengthen your spine, then hinge forward over the front leg from the hips
  4. Rest your hands on the floor, your shin, or blocks
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then rise slowly and change sides
ea_pyramid_pose_parsvottanasana

Pyramid Pose Blocks

Yoga

PurposeBlocks under the hands bring the floor up to you, so the back can stay flat instead of rounding to reach. A flat back is what makes the hamstring stretch work at all, so this is the better version for most people.

  1. Place a block on each side of your front foot
  2. Step the other foot back a leg's length and square your hips forward
  3. Keep both legs straight and lengthen through the spine
  4. Hinge from the hips and rest your hands on the blocks
  5. Hold for thirty seconds with a flat back, then change sides
ea_pyramid_pose_blocks

Pyramid Pose Calf Blocks

Yoga

PurposeRaising the front toes on a block adds a calf stretch on top of the hamstring one, so the whole back of the leg lengthens together. Useful for anyone whose ankles limit their squat.

  1. Place a block under the ball of the front foot so the toes are raised
  2. Step the back foot away a leg's length with both legs straight
  3. Square your hips and lengthen your spine
  4. Hinge forward from the hips over the front leg
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, feeling the calf and hamstring together, then swap
ea_pyramid_pose_calf_blocks ankle

Pyramid Prayer

Yoga

PurposeAdding the prayer hands behind the back turns a hamstring stretch into a shoulder and wrist opener as well. Two very different tight areas addressed in one shape, which is efficient if time is short.

  1. Bring your palms together behind your back with the fingers pointing up
  2. Step one foot forward a leg's length and square your hips
  3. Keep both legs straight and lengthen your spine
  4. Hinge forward over the front leg, keeping the palms pressed together
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, then rise and change sides
ea_pyramid_prayer

Reclining Pigeon Pose

Yoga

PurposeThe same hip stretch as pigeon but lying down, where the floor supports your spine and you control the pressure with your hands. Far kinder to the knees, and the right version for a stiff or sore back.

  1. Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet on the floor
  2. Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the knee
  3. Thread one hand through the gap and clasp the back of the supporting thigh
  4. Draw that leg toward your chest, letting the crossed knee open outward
  5. Hold for a minute, keeping your head on the floor, then change sides
ea_reclining_pigeon_pose hip

Restful Cow Face Pose Legs

Yoga

PurposeStacking the knees stretches the outside of both hips at once and can be held for several minutes without effort. A position to settle into at the end of a session rather than to work at.

  1. Sit on the floor and bend one knee, drawing the foot toward the opposite hip
  2. Stack the other knee directly on top and bring that foot to the other hip
  3. Sit on a cushion if your knees are high or your back rounds
  4. Rest your hands on the top knee and sit tall
  5. Hold for one to three minutes, then swap which knee is on top
ea_restful_cow_face_pose_legs

Reverse Prayer

Yoga

PurposePressing the palms together behind the back demands more from the shoulders and wrists than almost any other stretch. If it is not accessible, holding opposite elbows behind the back does the same job more gently.

  1. Stand or sit tall with your shoulders rolled back and down
  2. Bring both hands behind your back with the fingers pointing down
  3. Rotate the hands until the fingers point up and the palms meet
  4. Press the palms together and draw the elbows back to open the chest
  5. Hold for twenty to thirty seconds, breathing steadily
ea_reverse_prayer

Revolved Side Angle Pose with Prayer Hands

Yoga

PurposeCombines a lunge with a deep twist, so the legs work while the spine rotates against the resistance of the thigh. It reaches rotation range that a seated twist cannot, because the hips are locked by the stance.

  1. Step into a lunge with the back heel lifted and the front knee over the ankle
  2. Bring your palms together in front of your chest
  3. Turn your torso toward the front leg and hook the opposite elbow outside that knee
  4. Press the elbow and knee against each other to deepen the turn
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind and change sides
ea_revolved_side_angle_pose_with_prayer_hands

Revolved Side Angle Pose with Prayer Hands Beginner

Yoga

PurposeThe same twist with the back knee down, which removes the balance demand so you can concentrate on the rotation itself. This is where to start before attempting the full version.

  1. Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, both bent to ninety degrees
  2. Bring your palms together at your chest and sit tall
  3. Turn your ribs toward the front leg
  4. Rest the opposite elbow on the outside of the front knee and press gently
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, then unwind and swap sides
ea_revolved_side_angle_pose_with_prayer_hands_beginner

Runners Lunge

Yoga

PurposeOpens the front of the back hip and the inside of the front one, which is the pair that limits stride length in running. Ninety seconds of this before a run changes how the first kilometre feels.

  1. From all fours, step one foot forward to the outside of the same-side hand
  2. Straighten the back leg and press through the heel or rest the knee down
  3. Lower onto your forearms or keep the hands flat, whichever you can hold
  4. Let the front hip sink toward the floor and keep the chest open
  5. Hold for thirty to sixty seconds, then change sides
ea_runners_lunge hipknee

Scorpion Twist Pose

Yoga

PurposeA face-down twist that stretches the front of the shoulder and chest on one side while opening the hip on the other. It reaches two very different tight areas in a single position, without any strength demand.

  1. Lie face down with both arms out wide at shoulder height, palms down
  2. Bend one knee and lift that leg
  3. Reach it across your body toward the opposite hand, letting the hip roll
  4. Keep both shoulders pressing toward the floor as the leg crosses
  5. Hold for thirty seconds, breathing, then unwind slowly and change sides
ea_scorpion_twist_pose wrist

Side Lying Parsva Savasana Variation

Yoga

PurposeA resting position on the side that requires nothing from you at all, used to finish a session or to calm the breathing down. Rest is part of training, not the absence of it.

  1. Lie on one side with your knees bent and stacked
  2. Rest your head on your lower arm or a cushion
  3. Place the top arm wherever it is comfortable — in front of you or along your side
  4. Let your whole body soften and stop holding any position
  5. Breathe slowly for one to five minutes, then roll up carefully
ea_side_lying_parsva_savasana_variation hip

Wild Thing Pose

Yoga

PurposeA large chest and shoulder opener done from a side plank, which also asks the glutes to hold the hips high. It is the most extended front-body position in common practice — go into it warm, never cold.

  1. Start in a side plank on one hand with the feet stacked
  2. Step the top foot back behind you and place it flat on the floor
  3. Press through both feet and lift your hips high
  4. Sweep the top arm overhead and let your chest open toward the ceiling
  5. Hold for fifteen to twenty seconds, then come down carefully and change sides
ea_wild_thing_pose

Yoga Flow Sequences Sun Salutations

Yoga

PurposeA sequence rather than a single pose: it moves the whole spine through flexion and extension while warming the shoulders, hips and hamstrings. The most efficient general warm-up there is when you have five minutes and no equipment.

  1. Stand tall, then reach both arms overhead on an inhale
  2. Fold forward over your legs, then lift halfway with a flat back
  3. Step or jump back to a plank, lower down, and lift the chest into a gentle backbend
  4. Push the hips up and back into a downward dog and hold for a breath
  5. Step the feet back to the hands, fold, and rise to standing — then repeat the round
